---
title: "waper"
subtitle: "A Rossby Wave Packet trackER"
---

`waper` identifies Rossby wave packets (RWPs) in a meridional wind field and tracks them
through time. Identification is purely spatial and graph-based: for each time step it
detects alternating maxima and minima, clusters them, builds an association graph, prunes
it, and extracts RWP paths. Tracking then connects features across consecutive time steps
by an energy-weighted overlap: alongside each timestep's feature raster the package burns a
raster of squared amplitude around the RWP extrema, and the weight on an edge between a
feature at one step and a feature at the next is the sum of `sqrt(E_prev * E_curr)` over the
pixels the two share, divided by the larger of the two features' total energies — so the
association is driven by the energetic cores rather than by the extent of the footprints.
No spectral envelope is computed at any stage.

The method is described in [Pandey, Monteiro & Natarajan
(2020)](https://doi.org/10.1175/MWR-D-20-0014.1), *An Integrated Geometric and Topological
Approach for the Identification and Visual Analysis of Rossby Wave Packets*, Monthly
Weather Review 148(8), 3139–3157. See [Algorithm](algorithm.md) for what the package
currently implements, and the [API reference](api/index.qmd) for the public interface.

## Installation

`waper` is installed from a source checkout. It requires Python >= 3.11; CI tests it on
Python 3.11 and 3.12 on Linux.

Its geospatial dependencies build against compiled libraries (VTK, PROJ, GEOS), so install
them from conda-forge into a fresh environment first, in a single command, so the solver
can resolve them together:

```bash
mamba create -n waper -c conda-forge python=3.12 \
    geovista vtk xarray networkx rasterio scikit-learn tqdm
mamba activate waper
```

Then install the package itself from your clone:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JoyMonteiro/waper.git
cd waper
pip install -e .
```

Add the `dev` extra (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`) for the test and lint tooling, or the
`docs` extra to build this site.

## Usage

```python
import xarray as xr
from waper import Waper

ds = xr.open_dataset("v_winds_300mb.nc")

w = Waper(
    data_array=ds,
    scalar_name="v",
    latitude_label="latitude",
    longitude_label="longitude",
    time_label="time",
)
w.identify_rwps()
w.track_rwps()
```

`Waper` exposes further parameters controlling clipping, extrema detection, the latitude
band searched, and how aggressively the graphs and tracks are pruned; they are listed in
the [API reference](api/index.qmd).
